cards.explanation: The answer is them and their children and grandchildren. Moses, Israel's leader, says it's “…you and your children and grandchildren…” who may fear the LORD all the days of their lives (Deuteronomy 6:2). Three generations in one sentence, friends. Nobody gets left on the bench.

The answer is True. Moses says to be careful to observe these commands “…so that you may prosper and multiply greatly in a land flowing with milk and honey…” (Deuteronomy 6:3). He adds that this is just as the LORD, the God of their fathers, has promised. Milk and honey, friends. Sounds like a good place to set up an oven.

The answer is that He is the only LORD. Moses says, “Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is One.” (Deuteronomy 6:4). He opens with the word Hear, so Israel is told to listen up. Later in this same sermon he says to serve Him only (Deuteronomy 6:13).

The answer is all. Moses says to love the LORD your God “…with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength.” (Deuteronomy 6:5). Look at how he builds it, friends. Heart gets all, soul gets all, strength gets all. No corner of the cookie box gets left empty.

The answer is children. Moses says “…you shall teach them diligently to your children…” (Deuteronomy 6:7). And diligently means he's not asking for a once-a-year talk. These words get passed down on purpose, friends.

The answer is False. Moses never says Sabbath here. He says to speak of them “…when you sit at home and when you walk along the road, when you lie down and when you get up.” (Deuteronomy 6:7). That's every kind of day, friends, from sunrise to bedtime.

The answer is on their hands and foreheads. Moses says “Tie them as reminders on your hands and bind them on your foreheads.” (Deuteronomy 6:8). Those are the spots your eyes and hands are on all day. Hard to forget something you keep bumping into.

The answer is True. Moses says, “Write them on the doorposts of your houses and on your gates.” (Deuteronomy 6:9). Doorposts AND gates, friends. It's like sticking a note on the front door so you won't forget your keys, because the words go where your eyes will land.

The answer is wells and vineyards and olive groves. Moses says the land has “…wells that you did not dig, and with vineyards and olive groves that you did not plant…” (Deuteronomy 6:11). Somebody else did the digging and the planting, friends. And Israel is the one who gets to enjoy them.

The answer is to forget the LORD. Moses warns, “…be careful not to forget the LORD who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.” (Deuteronomy 6:12). He says it right after talking about eating and being satisfied. I'd say an oven full of warm cookies can make anybody forget a few things.

The answer is True. Moses says “Fear the LORD your God, serve Him only, and take your oaths in His name.” (Deuteronomy 6:13). Fear, serve and swear, all pointed at Him. That's a full list for one verse, friends.

The answer is the peoples around them. Moses says “Do not follow other gods, the gods of the peoples around you.” (Deuteronomy 6:14). That's the peoples living around Israel, friends. Their gods are the ones not to follow.

The answer is test. Moses says, “Do not test the LORD your God…” (Deuteronomy 6:16). He points back to a place Israel already knew, Massah. There the people tested the LORD, saying, “Is the LORD among us or not?” (Exodus 17:7). I think Moses is telling them not to go down that road again.

The answer is that it goes well and they possess the land. Moses says to do what is right and good “…so that it may be well with you and that you may enter and possess the good land…” (Deuteronomy 6:18). It's the good land the LORD swore to give their fathers. That's the reason Moses gives, friends.

The answer is True. Moses speaks of “…driving out all your enemies before you, as the LORD has said.” (Deuteronomy 6:19). Notice he says ALL. Not some, not most, ALL. I can't even promise all the crumbs make it off my counter, friends, and Moses is talking about a whole land.

The answer is slaves. “We were slaves of Pharaoh in Egypt…” (Deuteronomy 6:21). Pharaoh was the king of Egypt (Exodus 6:11). Notice the son asks about the laws and the answer starts with a story. It starts with where they came from, and then comes the mighty hand that brought them out.

The answer is land. “…He brought us out from there to lead us in and give us the land that He had sworn to our fathers.” (Deuteronomy 6:23). Out of Egypt and into the land, friends. That's the answer the son hears.

The answer is True. The answer to the son says “…the LORD commanded us to observe all these statutes and to fear the LORD our God, that we may always be prosperous and preserved, as we are to this day.” (Deuteronomy 6:24). Prosperous and preserved, friends. And it adds as we are to this day.
